gap: No result ChatGPT got states a single lab-measured figure for any screen: the one candidate a named reviewer has measured, the ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK, reached 205 cd/m² against ASUS's 250 cd/m² claim and covered 62% of sRGB (Sasha Muller, Expert Reviews, 14 Aug 2025), and no named reviewer I could find has measured the SIAVIALA, UPERFECT, FOPO S1 or Mobile Pixels Fold.
standout_why: I opened theofficejournal.com (under-150), dejaflow.com, twelvetabs.com, dupple.com and deal.ai on 2026-11-21. All five print only maker or listing figures (300 nits, 72% NTSC, 100% sRGB) and none attributes a measurement to anyone. The Office Journal and Dupple say outright they did not test, and twelvetabs says its guide was written by AI from listings. deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403, so I could not compare it. The measured-versus-claimed gap for the ASUS, and the absence of any lab data for the attachable extenders, appears on none of them.
decides: It does not change the pick; it changes how the page states brightness and colour. Every under-$150 attachable row (FOPO S1, Mobile Pixels Fold, SIAVIALA, UPERFECT) stands on maker figures only, so those cells should be labelled as the maker's claim. The one measured candidate, the freestanding ASUS MB169CK, came in 18% under its claimed brightness (205 vs 250 cd/m²) with 62% sRGB: fine for documents indoors, wrong for colour work. Notebookcheck's 2022 test of an older FOPO 12-inch attachable pair (193.1 cd/m², 247:1) is the only lab test of any FOPO extender I found. It is a different model from the S1, so it supports a caution about attachable panels, not a figure for our row. Measurements favour neither of our rows over the rivals.
